item.title: France boosts police to prevent repeat riots
item.media:keywords: France, Police, protests, Laurent Nunez, Violence
item.description: Heavily armed squads and elite teams will reinforce regular units to reassure the public that the government retains control of the streets
item.content:encoded:
France will deploy 70,000 police at nationwide protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday, looking to prevent a repeat of the violence and looting that shocked the country last weekend.

Elite security teams and heavily armed mobile squads will be mobilised alongside regular units in a show of force aimed at dispelling fears the government has lost control of the streets.

"We will be uncompromising with rioters, looters and all those who commit acts of violence," Nunez told reporters, adding that "ultra-left" groups had been urging activists online to target public buildings and unleash more lawlessness.

"We are not talking about a nice, friendly demonstration," Nunez said. "We are ready for tomorrow. We will be extremely vigilant, extremely firm, and we will let absolutely nothing pass."

Shooting Spree Near Paris Adds to Tensions

Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the streets in recent weeks, but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have taken advantage of the dispute to sow chaos.

Some far-right politicians have blamed migrants and radical Islam for the turmoil. President Emmanuel Macron has dismissed such accusations.

Ratcheting up the tensions, a man, who officials suspect was motivated by Islamophobic hatred, opened fire from a car west of Paris on Friday, killing one person and wounding four others, including a 12-year-old girl.

"(It was) objectively a racist attack," said local mayor Ali Rabeh, blaming far-right rhetoric for inflaming tensions.

Police have authorised only one union demonstration in Paris on Saturday, rejecting requests for rallies lodged by France's main student union, UNEF, and the Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that first emerged in 2018.

Many French cities beyond Paris have also banned protests but the second largest city, Marseille, rescinded an earlier restriction order and said it would allow a union demonstration.

UNEF said its rallies, which grew from high school protests last month against teacher shortages and shabby facilities, would go ahead regardless.

Marylise Leon, the general secretary of the CFDT, one of the nation's largest trade unions, criticised Macron for not sanctioning more demonstrations.

"It's counterproductive because there is a lot of anger, a lot of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to," she told French broadcaster TF1. "It's not for the president to decide who can legitimately request to protest."

Far-Right Congress a Possible Flashpoint

Nunez said 10,000 more police would be on the streets than a week ago, while mounted police, helicopters, drones and anti-drone systems would be deployed across the country.

Armoured vehicles and water cannon vehicles would also be available, while curfews imposed in some sensitive areas this past week would remain in force.

Authorities are also concerned that the annual congress of Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally in Orleans this weekend could become a flashpoint, with left-wing and anti-racist groups announcing counter-demonstrations.

The upsurge of violence has boosted poll ratings for Le Pen, who is the frontrunner for next year's presidential election. She has portrayed the unrest as evidence of a collapse in state authority.

Fears of renewed turmoil prompted several of Paris' best-known cultural institutions, including the Louvre, the Musée d'Orsay and the Opera House, to close all day on Saturday.

Paris St Germain's home Ligue 1 soccer match with Olympique Lyonnais was shifted from Sunday to Monday over security concerns. However, an NFL regular-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints is still scheduled to be played in Paris on Sunday, although US President Donald Trump suggested it should be cancelled.

Business groups also urged shops to stay shut after some 3,000 stores and businesses were ransacked last weekend.

Alain Di Crescenzo, the president of France's chamber of commerce, said some shopkeepers were arming themselves with baseball bats, crowbars and shotguns to protect their properties. But he urged them not to turn to violence.

"It’s extremely worrying," he told Europe 1 radio. "It's not their job to do that. It would add suffering onto suffering."

The social turbulence has intensified scrutiny of France's economic outlook and ratings agency Moody's is widely expected to cut the French credit rating on Friday, underscoring concern that the government had not reined in public spending.

item.title: Carrick accepts blame for United slump
item.media:keywords: Manchester United, Michael Carrick, Champions League, Premier League
item.description: He describes the loss in Italy as one of the most painful nights of his tenure
item.content:encoded:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick mounted an impassioned defence of his leadership on Friday, accepting responsibility for the club's collapse in form and saying he remains convinced he can lead the team out of their current crisis.

Carrick's position is under increasing pressure after United extended their winless run to seven matches in all competitions with Wednesday's humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como leaving them 20th in the table with three points.

Before taking questions ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, Carrick delivered an emotional opening statement, acknowledging supporters' frustrations and the scale of the challenge facing him.

"Recently, we haven't had a good time. I think that's pretty obvious. So I totally accept what we're going through at the moment," he said.

"We had five months of relative success (last season) in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things I was seeing and that we were doing as a team," he said.

"We haven't done well enough lately. We've had a spell that we're really not happy with."

Carrick described the loss in Italy as one of the most painful nights of his tenure.

"Wednesday was a bad night. It was a bad night for a lot of reasons. It hurt a lot," he said. "It obviously hurt me to see us play that way. As I said after the game, it was really unacceptable."

The defeat intensified scrutiny of Carrick after captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to question United's tactical approach in his post-match comments.

Dressing Rooms Cracks?

Asked whether public criticism from players suggested cracks within the dressing room, Carrick rejected any suggestion the squad was split.

He also sidestepped questions over Fernandes' future as captain and declined to reveal whether he had held talks with the Portugal midfielder following the defeat.

Instead, he stressed that his priority was restoring an identity that has disappeared from the side in recent weeks.

"My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show," Carrick said.

"We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I'm fully aware of and definitely doing something about."

He reserved special mention for United's fans, many of whom travelled to Como only to watch their side suffer the heaviest defeat of his reign.

"The supporters are a huge part of this football club. They have to make the effort and the time and money they spend, to feel how we all felt on Wednesday was a tough moment," he said.

Defiant Tone

Despite growing speculation about his future, Carrick struck a defiant tone, saying he remained confident United could rediscover the energy and connection that characterised last season's performances.

He took over in January 2026 after the sacking of Ruben Amorim and oversaw a remarkable turnaround, steering United to a top-three finish and Champions League qualification.

"For them (the fans) to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year ... is something we need to get back to. We will get back to it. I fully believe that," said Carrick.

Former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager Antonio Conte is among the names linked with United's managerial job, although the 57-year-old Italian said on Friday he had not had any negotiations "at an advanced stage" with any club.

Carrick acknowledged that United had lost their way but said responsibility rested squarely with him.

He ended his opening remarks by saying it was his duty to guide the club back on course, describing his role as "holding the umbrella for me to get wet and everyone else to stay dry".

United are 13th in the Premier League standings on seven points, while Bournemouth are a point behind them in 15th.

item.title: 2 Bangladeshis jailed in Canada for ‘trafficking, raping’ woman
item.media:keywords: Canada, Jail, Bangladeshi men, Trafficking, sexual exploitation
item.description: Prosecutor says one man had exploited the woman “for his own sexual gratification”, including assaults involving violence
item.content:encoded:
A Canadian court has sentenced two Bangladeshi men to prison for trafficking and exploiting a Bangladeshi woman, with one of them also convicted of repeatedly raping her.

Md Masum, 45, was sentenced to 14 years in prison, while Sohel Haider, 56, received a four-year term, CBC News reports.

Both men were convicted of human trafficking earlier this year. Masum was also found guilty of three sexual assaults, which Judge Miguel Martinez described in simpler language as “rapes”.

The court also ordered Sohel to pay the woman $5,885 in restitution for unpaid wages and Masum to pay $12,268.

The woman went to Canada as a temporary foreign worker. According to CBC News, she first worked at Sohel's restaurant in Gull Lake and later at Masum's restaurant in Tisdale.

She was underpaid, made to work long hours six days a week and did not have proper work permits, CBC News reports.

The charges covered the period from Aug 1, 2022, to Mar 31, 2023. She later obtained a permit to work at a restaurant in Elrose and fled with help from people who were concerned about her situation.

In a victim impact statement, the woman said the men had “destroyed her life”.

“I can't forget them. They stopped my dream. They destroyed my life. They ruined my honour, my future, my family, my career,” she told CBC News.

She also said gossip about her in Bangladesh had damaged her family's honour. Once independent, she now depends on others, and questioned her decision to come to Canada, where she felt like a product sold to a customer, CBC News reports.

Crown prosecutor Leslie Dunning had sought a 15-year sentence for Masum on one human trafficking count and three sexual assault counts, and five-and-a-half years for Sohel. Dunning argued the men were in positions of trust and controlled “virtually every aspect of her life”.

Masum had exploited the woman “for his own sexual gratification”, including assaults involving violence, the prosecutor said.

Masum's lawyer Zachary Carter sought a sentence of seven to nine years, describing it as “substantial”. Sohel's lawyer Chris Gratton argued for the four-year mandatory minimum.

item.title: Iran details plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes
item.media:keywords: Iran, undersea cables, Gulf, US, Israel
item.description: Official says Iran will aim to prolong communications outages by preventing post-attack repairs
item.content:encoded:
Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters.

Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington collapses.

The two Iranian security officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, gave few details and did not say how or where exactly Tehran would carry out such attacks. But one of them said Iran would aim to prevent repairs after any attacks to prolong disruptions to communications, including internet connections.

"If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines ... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one of the officials said.

The official warned Washington not to "play with fire", and said Iran had full access to the undersea cables and could easily destroy them.

Yadollah Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure came under attack.

Undersea cables carry around 99 percent of global internet traffic, according to the International Telecommunication Union, a UN agency. But the global impact of such attacks by Iran could be limited as less than 1 percent of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz, said Alan Mauldin, research director at telecommunications research firm TeleGeography.

The strait separates Iran and Oman, linking the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.

The US Department of State and Iran's Foreign Ministry did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment on the Iranian security officials' remarks. There was no immediate comment from Gulf states.

'Stronger Response'

The plans for possible attacks on undersea cables reflect a conviction in Iran's leadership that a renewed US military campaign would have to be met with a stronger response than before.

Top security official Mohsen Rezaei warned this month that US-linked digital infrastructure across the Gulf, including data centres and AI facilities, could be targeted in a renewed conflict.

Washington's Gulf allies have invested heavily in such infrastructure and they "should hold Washington, not Tehran, responsible for any damage to undersea cables," the second Iranian security official said.

Alex Vatanka, director of the Iran program at West Asia Institute in Washington, said such threats were intended to deter renewed conflict and put pressure on Washington by making Gulf governments and US companies fear for their investments in the region.

"Tehran wants Gulf states and corporate executives to press (US President Donald) Trump over the risks his policies pose to their investment plans," said Vatanka.

Multiple cable cuts could slow internet services and disrupt financial transactions, e-commerce and cloud computing, analysts said. The impact would depend on how operators rerouted traffic and the capacity available on alternative connections, Mauldin said.

Restoring connections during wartime could be difficult, experts said, and higher insurance costs and delays in obtaining permits to enter territorial waters could further complicate repairs.

The Red Sea could offer a more significant target than the Strait of Hormuz, particularly if Iran had support from its Houthi allies in Yemen, though Tehran has made no public statement indicating it plans to target cables there.

The Red Sea carries data between Europe, East Africa and Asia, with capacity routed through it accounting for about 3 percent of global international demand and around 10 percent of traffic travelling between regions, Mauldin said.

Gulf governments have been investing heavily in technology to diversify beyond oil and become global artificial intelligence hubs, deepening ties with US technology firms.

Iranian strikes directly hit two Amazon Web Services facilities in the UAE in March and damaged infrastructure near one of its facilities in Bahrain. The IRGC named US tech companies including Microsoft, Google, Apple and Nvidia as legitimate targets at the height of the war in March.

Land-based connections can provide alternative routes for internet traffic, and Gulf states and US technology companies are investing in additional infrastructure to improve resilience.

Microsoft plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea and terrestrial connectivity across West Asia by 2030.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire in flood-hit city
item.media:keywords: Melania Trump, ceasefire, Russia, Ukraine, Oleshky, food crisis
item.description: Ukraine's top negotiator says humanitarian operations would start once a ceasefire was in place
item.content:encoded:
US first lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin next Thursday, the White House said on Friday.

The chief of staff of Russian forces, Valery Gerasimov, said on the Defence Ministry's Telegram channel that Russian troops would halt fire from 4am local time (0100 GMT) on Tuesday to allow for the humanitarian operation to start.

Residents of the southern Ukrainian city, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported a deepening food crisis.

"Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," a White House statement said.

Ukraine's top negotiator, David Arakhamia, said on Telegram that the humanitarian operation would start once a ceasefire was in place.

He said the accord, the result of a long process involving Melania Trump and Pope Leo, would set up a humanitarian corridor for residents to leave and allow assistance into the town.

In Moscow, the Kremlin welcomed the agreement. It praised Melania Trump's role in securing the agreement and said President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin had discussed details.

The Kremlin said earlier this week that work was under way to ease the humanitarian situation in Oleshky after Putin told the pope he was ready to cooperate on the issue.

The development comes as President Trump pressures Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to reach an agreement with Putin to end the war, which began when Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

First Lady Has Sought To Help Ukrainian Children

Melania Trump has been active in trying to get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families.

"The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water," Melania Trump said in the statement.

The ceasefire will allow non-military teams from both countries to visit residents in their homes and coordinate transportation for those wishing to evacuate to either Russia or Ukraine, with an unnamed American media organisation accompanying the teams to document the process, the first lady said.

Newsmax, a right-leaning news outlet, said in a report that its cameras would be granted "exclusive access to document the effort."

Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, has a remaining population of 1,700 to 2,000 people — primarily elderly residents, along with about 50 children — down from roughly 24,000 before the war, the White House said. About 90 percent of the city was flooded following the 2023 destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, according to the White House.

The statement said Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localised ceasefire.

"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” Melania Trump said.

item.title: Crude bomb blast outside old Ramna Police Station
item.media:keywords: crude bomb, blast, explosive, Ramna Police Station, Dhaka
item.description: Two people on a motorcycle came to the spot, threw the improvised explosive, and drove off, police say
item.content:encoded:
A crude bomb has exploded in front of the old Ramna Police Station in Dhaka’s Bailey Road.

The blast occurred around 8pm on Friday, according to Sheikh Jahidul Islam, deputy commissioner of the police’s Ramna Division.

He said two people on a motorcycle came to the spot, threw the improvised explosive, and drove off.

There were no casualties, Jahidul said.

“Police are examining CCTV footage to identify those involved,” he added.

item.title: Bus torched after 2 die in Ctg road crash
item.media:keywords: Bus, autorickshaw, crash, Chattogram, torched, Arson, protest
item.description: Traffic returns to normal after police go to the scene and remove protesters
item.content:encoded:
Two autorickshaw passengers have been killed after the vehicle was rammed by a bus in Chattogram.

The accident occurred on the Chattogram-Cox’s Bazar Highway in Satkania’s Nayakhal around 8pm on Friday. Afterwards, protesters blocked the road and set the bus on fire, police said.

The incident brought traffic to a standstill on the road for about an hour and a half.

Nurul Absar, chief of Dohazari Highway Police Station, said: “Traffic began moving normally around 9:30pm after police went to the scene and removed the protesters from the road.”

Locals said that a bus headed from Satkania’s Keranihat to Chattogram City veered out of control in Nayakhal and rammed a parked motorcycle and an autorickshaw. The passengers on the autorickshaw were seriously injured in the crash.

item.title: Mourinho seeks Clasico turning point at Real
item.media:keywords: Spain, El Clasico, Real Madrid, Jose Mourinho, Barcelona
item.description: The manager’s every move will draw attention during the heated Clasico following memories of his previous fiery spell at Real Madrid
item.content:encoded:
Spain's biggest football fixture arrives on Sunday night at Camp Nou with as many as 14 new faces that could make their Clasico debuts, but the return of Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho to the fixture will attract the most attention of all.

Real Madrid and Barcelona both made six signings in the close season, while the Catalan club have promoted two youth academy products to their senior squad, injecting the tie with a fresh crop of players keen to leave their mark on the rivalry.

Among them is Brazilian striker Gabriel Jesus, who joined Barcelona from Arsenal in September.

"Barcelona against Real Madrid is, without a doubt, amongst the biggest in the world," Jesus told Reuters on Thursday ahead of the first meeting between the two sides this season.

"It really is a dream to play in the Clasico for the first time. I've never made a secret of my desire to one day wear the Barcelona shirt and that goal includes playing in El Clasico."

Jesus is no stranger to facing Real Madrid, having scored three times against Los Blancos in four matches for Manchester City.

"They were memorable Champions League clashes, including a goal at the Bernabeu," he said.

The 29-year-old Jesus grew up 8,797km away in Sao Paulo, and he could line up alongside Xavi Espart, who was born in Barcelona and came through their youth academy. One of nine academy graduates in their squad, Espart highlighted the implications of the match both in the standings and in the rivalry.

"The truth is, it’s going to be a war. We will go all out, it’s a Clasico," Espart told DAZN on Thursday.

"You always have to give 100 percent, now we have the chance to extend our lead and we'll fight to the death."

Victory for Barcelona would extend the gap in LaLiga between the two teams to nine points, a sizable margin to overcome. Should Real come away with a win, it would not only halve the current six-point gap, but provide a much-needed confidence boost for a side that has lost six of the last seven Clasicos.

Mourinho’s Return

At the other end of the experience scale to Espart is Mourinho. The 63-year-old is a veteran of 27 matches against Barcelona and 17 Clasicos on the Real bench.

Real Madrid President Florentino Perez first appointed Mourinho as manager in 2010 to compete with Pep Guardiola's Barcelona, and he will hope the Portuguese can wrest the LaLiga title back to the Bernabeu for a second time.

Mourinho's first spell at Real coincided with arguably the most heated encounters in the modern history of El Clasico, and there will be numerous cameras trained on his every move at Camp Nou on Sunday.

The Portuguese manager won just once in his first 10 Clasicos, but went unbeaten in his final five games against Barcelona, recording three victories.

Recovering the winning formula against Barcelona may well represent a turning point in Mourinho's second Real Madrid tenure, after two losses in their opening nine LaLiga games and frequent whistles from their own fans during home games.

item.title: 300 tourists rush out amid Cox’s Bazar hotel fire
item.media:keywords: The Sea Princess, Bangladesh, Tourists, hotel, Cox’s Bazar
item.description: The fire started on the ground-floor parking lot at The Sea Princess Hotel on Friday afternoon
item.content:encoded:
Within a week of a fire at a Cox’s Bazar tourist resort that claimed 10 lives, another fire has broken out at a hotel in the district.

However, no casualties have been reported in the latest incident.

The fire started on the ground-floor parking of The Sea Princess Hotel in Sugondha Point in the beach town on Friday afternoon, according to Dolon Acharya, senior station officer of the Cox’s Bazar Fire Service and Civil Defence.

He said a unit from the nearby Fire Service station quickly reached the spot after the fire was reported. However, hotel authorities had brought the fire under control before its arrival.

Dolon said it is initially believed the fire started from a short circuit in a generator. He added that no one was injured in the incident.

The hotel's Managing Director Abdul Kader said there were more than 300 tourists in the hotel when the fire broke out. However, everyone is safe, he added.

Kader said that the hotel has adequate firefighting facilities and it was possible to avoid a major incident due to quick work by the staff.

Although there were no casualties in the fire, some parts of the parking area, including the generator, were damaged.

item.title: China ‘opposes’ arms race in space
item.media:keywords: China, weaponisation, space, arms, space governance
item.description: Space arms race and battlefield ambitions threaten global space security, the document says
item.content:encoded:
China on Friday released a document detailing its official position on "space governance" that reaffirms its opposition to the weaponisation of outer space and to a space arms race.

● China opposes the weaponisation and militarisation of outer space and is against its use "for activities that harm other countries' sovereignty, security, or development interests," according to the document, which was released by its foreign ministry

● China opposes offensive military policies in outer space and calls for "every possible effort to prevent an arms race in outer space", it says

● The document adds that "the risk of an arms race in outer space and the trend toward turning it into a battlefield have become the greatest threats and challenges to space security"

● The document calls for regulating commercial space activities and says China encourages "the development of the space economy". It says commercial space activities should "not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of other countries, and in particular avoid unlawfully intervening in other countries' armed conflicts and internal affairs"

● The document also calls for outer space to be explored and used for peaceful purposes. It says all countries' right to access, explore and use space should be safeguarded

item.title: Shein to pay $100mn to settle US FTC probe
item.media:keywords: Shein, Investigation, US FTC, customer complaints, settlement
item.description: FTC records show consumers filed over 12,000 complaints about more than $11 million in purchases between January 2020 and June 2026
item.content:encoded:
Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein has agreed to pay $100 million to settle an investigation by the US Federal Trade Commission over delivery delays and other customer complaints, a source with direct knowledge told Reuters on Friday.

The settlement, equivalent to 44 percent of Shein's second-quarter profit, is the latest to hit the online fast-fashion retailer facing a regulatory and tax crackdown in Europe and the US that has slammed the brakes on its growth.

Shein, founded in China though headquartered in Singapore, said in a statement to Reuters that it had "reached a constructive outcome with the FTC", and that additional information would be shared soon. An FTC spokesperson declined to comment.

The company had warned in July filings for its Hong Kong IPO that the US probe could lead to significant fines.

Consumers filed more than 12,000 complaints about Shein over more than $11 million in purchases between January 2020 and June 2026, according to FTC records reviewed by Reuters.

At least some of those relate to shipping, with customers reporting to the FTC and Better Business Bureau that they never received packages that Shein had marked as delivered and that Shein customer service did not resolve the issue.

Reuters was not able to independently verify the substance of the complaints, or whether they were ultimately resolved.

Shein Shares Down 22 Percent From Listing Price

As well as selling its own-brand clothing, Shein's website also operates as a marketplace where third-party sellers offer everything from toys to household appliances and decor.

Shein shares have already dropped 22 percent from their Sept 1 listing price as investors have grasped the extent to which fees on e-commerce packages imposed by the European Union have dented its business there.

Jefferies analysts say Shein's app downloads across ten markets were down 42 percent in September versus a year ago.

Shein is also still under investigation by the European Commission over illegal products on its marketplace. It was fined €150 million ($168 million) by France's data protection authority over the improper use of cookies last year.

It's not the first time the US FTC has taken action against online retailers over deliveries.

US firm Fashion Nova was fined $9.3 million in 2020 for failing to meet shipping promises to customers and giving them gift cards instead of refunds.

Crocs Inc-owned Hey Dude was also fined $1.95 million in 2023 for failing to notify customers of shipping delays and suppressing negative reviews.

item.title: Saka will miss Everton clash, undergo more tests: Arteta
item.media:keywords: Arsenal, Bukayo Saka, Premier League, Everton, Mikel Arteta, Injury
item.description: The winger suffered a thigh injury during Arsenal’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern
item.content:encoded:
Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka will miss Saturday's Premier League match at home to Everton and have further tests on a thigh injury, manager Mikel Arteta said on Friday.

Saka, 25, suffered the issue 10 minutes into Arsenal’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday and was forced off the pitch.

"He's going for an MRI this afternoon because he had a lot of fluid in the area, so it was difficult to understand the severity of the injury. We will know tomorrow," Arteta told a press conference.

"We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. When a player is struggling to walk off the pitch and he's restricted in his movement, they are not good signs."

Following the England international's setback, Arteta also highlighted the strain the congested schedule places on players, calling for greater consideration from the governing bodies.

"If they can support the amount we are putting into these players, it would be really appreciated," he said.

"We have to play three times in less than six days, the games are so demanding, we are chasing until the last minute."

After facing Bayern and Everton, Arsenal will visit fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the League Cup fourth round on Tuesday.

item.title: China aims to stabilise new births
item.media:keywords: China, new births, Policy, population decline, birth rate
item.description: The State Council seeks to address the ageing population as it threatens social insurance system and economic growth
item.content:encoded:
China should offer more support to families to stabilise the number of new births, the cabinet said on Friday, as policymakers seek to address the country's population decline and record-low birth rate.

The government should refine policies including those related to marriage, childbirth, child-rearing and education, and optimise taxation, social security and housing to build a "fertility-friendly society", the State Council, or cabinet, said at a meeting, according to a readout aired by state television.

China's population fell for a fourth consecutive year in 2025, and experts have warned that it could decline further. The number of marriage registrations also dropped by about 7.5 percent in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year, according to official data.

The State Council's pledges are a sign that policymakers are concerned about the strain a shrinking and ageing population could put on the country's social insurance system and overall economic growth, which has been weighed down by weak domestic consumer demand.

"Population is the foundational condition for economic and social development," officials said in the meeting, calling for efforts so that "high-quality population development" could better support "high-quality economic and social development."

Authorities have in recent years stepped up fiscal support for boosting births, including rolling out a nationwide childcare subsidy programme and waiving or cutting pre-school tuition fees. They have also vowed to foster "positive attitudes towards marriage and childbearing."

The cabinet meeting also called for making basic public services more equal, echoing the government's moves to reform a decades-long household registration system so that workers who migrated from rural farms to cities can access more urban public services, including enrolling their children in public schools in the city.

item.title: Rally alleges govt neglect over Bangladeshis’ executions in Saudi
item.media:keywords: Expatriates, Saudi Arabia, execution, protest, Rally, Shahbagh, #shahbagh
item.description: “Within seven days, you must inform Bangladesh and the expatriate community what measures you are taking for those living abroad,” a protester says
item.content:encoded:
A rally has been held in Dhaka’s Shahbagh to protest the government's failure to prevent the execution of two Bangladeshis accused of engaging in "immoral activities" in Saudi Arabia.

Speakers criticised the government's actions in the event organised by a group called “Network for People's Action” outside the National Museum at 5pm on Friday.

Hasnat Qayyum, president of the Rastro Songskar Andolan, said at the rally: "When there is a situation where expatriates are killed without trial, without notice in the name of trial and their bodies are sent to Bangladesh, the questions that the people of Bangladesh are asking and the answers that one minister is giving are far more brutal than those of the previous fascist governments. Much more disgusting, much more offensive, much more insulting."

He said, “The government should clearly state what action they are taking against those from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs who have made such hateful statements. We want to see what action the government takes against them in the next seven days.

“If no action is taken, we will launch a movement against these ministers of this government on behalf of expatriates to remove them from their posts.”

Calling for measures to protect expatriates, he said: “Within seven days, you must inform Bangladesh and the expatriate community what measures you are taking for those living abroad, those who are suffering from cases against them, who are being harassed in various ways.”

“Otherwise, expatriates will reconsider whether they will send remittances.”

Tasnuva Zebin, organiser of the new political platform Alternatives, said: “The Saudi government did not consider the need for any kind of accountability before beheading two Bangladeshi citizens, did not consider the need to bring the matter before any kind of justice. We condemn this.

“…In a country where female workers and expatriate female workers from Bangladesh are tortured, raped and sent back to the country, how can that country, under any law, execute two Bangladeshi citizens by beheading them without informing Bangladesh? The Bangladeshi government must demand an answer to this, and we will force the Bangladeshi government to demand this answer from the Saudi government.”

Tasnuva asked why the two were in jail before the execution, but did not receive legal assistance from Bangladesh.

At the rally, she said: “Why has a Bangladeshi citizen been in jail since August 2023 without the consulate contacting them? Have they not received any kind of legal assistance? On the contrary, instead of protesting it or condemning it, our government is calling it a ‘corpse of sin.’”

Questioning the government’s steps to protect expatriates at the rally, researcher Maha Mirza said: “Expatriate workers are not just machines or animals who make money. It is the responsibility of the Bangladesh government, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare, to protect them. We want to ask: what is your plan? Please let us know.

"It is very important to bring about accountability, because we do not want another 30,000 coffins to return in the next four years.

“We want our expatriate worker brothers to get help from the embassy, get government help. Those who are in jail without committing any crime should have embassy staff go to them, list them, and make a database. We should be able to bring them back to the country properly.”

“And all the recruiting agencies that are guzzling hundreds of thousands of taka for fake documents while dumping expatriates abroad should be closed. If necessary, this entire process should be brought under government management."

item.title: Rabada, Smith renew rivalry before decider
item.media:keywords: Kagiso Rabada, Steve Smith, South Africa, Australia, Sports, Cricket, rivalry
item.description: Rabada returned after a long hamstring injury layoff to help South Africa win by an innings and 31 runs in the second Test in Gqeberha
item.content:encoded:
Quick bowler Kagiso Rabada's battles with Steve Smith sparked a combustible series the last time Australia played Tests in South Africa eight years ago and the pair have resumed their rivalry as the teams head for a decisive contest in Cape Town next week.

Rabada returned after a long hamstring injury layoff to help South Africa win by an innings and 31 runs in the second Test in Gqeberha on Thursday to square the three-match series and set up a potential thriller at Newlands, starting next Tuesday.

Rabada's four second-innings wickets included that of the 37-year-old Smith, who, surprisingly early in his innings, out of character and with Australia in dire straits, attempted an ill-fated hook to a bouncer and top-edged a catch to midwicket.

It was an injudicious decision from the former captain, who passed the milestone of 11,000 test runs at St George’s Park but made only three runs in the second innings as he looked out of sorts with a neck complaint.

Getting Best Player Out

“He wasn’t 100 percent fit in the game but we knew he had the ability to knuckle down and be the anchor for them; he’s done it for so long for Australia,” Rabada said in a TV interview.

“He’s a top-class player and you can put a lot more pressure on a team when you get their best player out, so he’ll always be a prized wicket playing against Australia.”

Rabada had also dismissed Smith at St George’s Park in 2018, the first of 11 wickets he took in that Test, but he collided with the Australian while celebrating taking his wicket and was handed a two-match ban, later downgraded to a fine.

The shoulder bump was among several incidents in an ill-spirited series that ended with the infamous ‘Sandpapergate’ ball-tampering scandal after which Smith was stripped of the captaincy and banned for 12 months by Cricket Australia.

No Grudges, Only Testosterone

Rabada, however, said there were no grudges and that it was part of intense competition.

“As an athlete you want to go out and express yourself. There’s no hate off the field or anything like that. It’s a bunch of top-performing athletes who’ve got testosterone to burn. It’s the heat of the moment,” the South African paceman said.

Smith has been back to Newlands since the scandal, playing in a T20 international two years after the incident, but this will be his first test at the venue since 2018.

Last month he said he had learned from the experience after being sent home in disgrace.

"It was certainly a difficult period, particularly the initial period a few days after," Smith told Sydney's Daily Telegraph.

"The mental state I was in was not great. That's somewhere I'd like not to get to again, but I certainly learned from that and have been able to move forward with my life. I've tried to kind of erase a lot of 2018 and what happened," he added.

"I can't remember a lot about the series. I've tried to block most of it out of my memory bank."

item.title: Madrasa torched over 'rape attempt' on student
item.media:keywords: vandalism, Mob, Arson, Teacher, rape attempt, Madrasa, Dhaka-Pabna train
item.description: “An investigation is under way to verify the allegation,” says Pabna Superintendent of Police Ali Ashraf
item.content:encoded:
A group of agitated locals has set fire to and vandalised a residential madrasa in Pabna Sadar Upazila after allegations that a rape attempt was made on a student. Police have detained a teacher of the madrasa over the incident.

Pabna Sadar Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Sanjay Kumar Saha said, “On Friday morning, local people set fire to and vandalised the ‘Nure Medina Mohila Madrasa’ in Kadamtala village of Dori Bhaudanga in Bharara Union of the Upazila.”

Teacher Md Abu Yusuf has been taken into police custody. He is a resident of Khalishpur village in Sadullapur Union of the Sadar Upazila, the inspector said.

Citing locals, police said there are 60 students at the madrasa, half of whom are residential students. On Thursday night, it was alleged that teacher Abu Yusuf tried to rape a student in the madrasa. The student then managed to escape to a nearby house, took shelter and informed her family members about the incident.

When news spread, tensions sparked in the area. Agitated locals detained the teacher and handed him over to the police.

On Friday morning, a group of the agitated locals vandalised and set fire to the madrasa. Police went to the scene and brought the situation under control when the incident was reported.

Law enforcers said the residential students were turned over to the custody of their guardians immediately after the incident.

Inspector Sanjay said, “Legal action against the teacher is under way. Additional police personnel have been deployed at the scene to maintain regular law and order in the area.”

Pabna Superintendent of Police Ali Ashraf said, “An investigation is under way to verify the allegation. Strict legal action will be taken soon, depending on the truth of the matter. In addition, the incident of vandalism and arson at the madrasa is also being investigated seriously.”

item.title: Oil spill off UAE coast prompts beach closures
item.media:keywords: UAE, oil spill, Environment, fuel, Tanker, West Asia, Beach
item.description: Containment operations have been launched and an environmental assessment was being carried out, authorities say
item.content:encoded:
The United Arab Emirates said efforts were under way on Friday to contain oil leaking from a tanker vessel offshore that prompted authorities to close beaches and warn fishermen to avoid the area.

Since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran, attacks on commercial vessels in Gulf shipping lanes have driven up security risks for maritime traffic and heightened fears over the conflict's environmental fallout.

The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said in a statement that containment operations had been launched and an environmental assessment was being carried out.

All beaches and coastal areas around the city of Umm Al Quwain had been temporarily closed until technical teams completed their assessments and determined the necessary safety and marine protection measures, it said.

The ministry also urged fishermen and other sea users to avoid affected areas and follow official instructions.

Authorities in Sharjah temporarily closed Al Hamriyah Beach, on the UAE's northern coast near the border with Umm Al Quwain, as a precaution, the Sharjah Government Media Bureau said.

Analyst Identifies Leaking Tanker As The Gem No.2

UAE authorities have not named the tanker involved in the incident or said what caused the spill. The environment ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Martin Kelly, CEO of Orbital Risk Intelligence, told Reuters that the spill was coming from a tanker called the Gem No.2 and analysts say satellite imagery from October 19 and 21 appears to show a significant oil slick from the tanker.

"The slick is considerably larger, covering approximately 160 km2, and looks to be coming from the ship," Leon Moreland, researcher at the Conflict and Environment Observatory, said.

"Furthermore, a slick this close to shore increases the chance it could impact nearby beaches and ecologically sensitive habitats," he said.

Shipping sources said on Oct 9 that the Gem No.2 was struck by an unidentified projectile 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera in the UAE, causing a fire that was later extinguished.

While no group claimed responsibility, maritime security sources told Reuters at the time that the incident occurred outside the Strait of Hormuz and pointed to a widening of risks for commercial shipping. Earlier that week, a tanker was also struck off the coast of Qatar inside the Gulf.

Spill Putting Coastal Infrastructure at Risk

Maritime intelligence firm Windward first identified the spill on Tuesday, writing in a post on X that a VLCC-sized vessel was leaking oil about 25 km (16 miles) off Umm Al Quwain.

Prevailing currents, it said at the time, could carry the slick southwest toward the UAE coastline.

"Windward's drift model shows it reaching Sharjah's and Ajman's desalination intakes and ports by (Oct 22–23) if the leak isn't stopped," it wrote on X.

Residents in some areas had posted on social media about strange odours. The ministry, however, said that odours reported in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain posed no health risks.

The smell was still pungent across Umm Al Quwain on Friday.

The UAE relies on desalination plants for most of its drinking water, and much of the economy — including ports and industrial facilities — is also located on the coast, making any contamination along its shoreline particularly sensitive.

The spill follows a separate tanker-related environmental incident in August, when oil from a tanker that ran aground off Oman began reaching the mainland coast.

item.title: 7 killed as gunmen open fire at church in Jordan
item.media:keywords: Jordan, church, West Asia, attack, gunmen, shooting
item.description: Interior minister says the attack had been carried out by "extremists"
item.content:encoded:
Seven people were killed and 34 injured on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan's Karak governorate, the head of the country's Public Security Directorate told reporters, in a rare attack on the country's Christian minority.

Speaking at a press conference in Karak, Major General Abdallah al-Maaytah said most of those wounded in the shooting at the Hamoud Church in Karak were still receiving treatment, and that the hunt for the attackers was ongoing.

Interior Minister Mazin Al Farrayeh said the attack had been carried out by "extremists", but that it was too early to tell whether they had any links to known groups either inside or outside Jordan.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility.

A video aired on Jordan's state-owned Al-Mamlaka television station that appeared to be from a security camera mounted on the church showed three people firing at it from a sidewalk and hiding behind trees and a low wall. The video showed the attackers then running towards the church's entrance. Reuters was able to verify the video from the entry path and wall surrounding the church, as well as other details.

Khaled Burqan, who was at the funeral, told Al-Mamlaka that dozens of people were present and that the gunmen opened fire on them for several minutes.

Ihab Ammareen, another witness, told the station that he saw bloodied people collapse on the floor after the attack. "People were crying, wailing, screaming — it's hard to describe," he told the station.

Blood Smeared on the Ground

Jordan's King Abdullah visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist".

"The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation. Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity," he said in a statement.

Reuters footage from the church after the attack showed blood smeared on the floor near its entrance, where security forces were deployed.

Such attacks are extremely rare in Jordan, which is relatively stable, though Jordanian authorities say they have repeatedly foiled attempted attacks by Islamist militants in recent years.

Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world.

Jordan's Minister of Endowments and Islamic Affairs Mohammad Khalayleh and several members of Jordan's parliament condemned the attack in comments to Al-Mamlaka.

The US ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz described it in a post on X as a "depraved and brutal attack on a house of worship."

Jordan was among the US allies in the region to be hit by Iranian attacks this year after the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.

item.title: France steps up security for new wave of protests
item.media:keywords: France, security, protests, Europe, riots, Arson, unrest, Asia-Europe routes, Air France
item.description: France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday
item.content:encoded:
France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday, accusing ultra-left groups of encouraging violence and looting after unrest shocked the country last weekend.

The government is seeking to prevent a repeat of last week's demonstrations that descended into riots, looting and arson in several cities, triggering widespread criticism of authorities for not preventing the mayhem.

"We will be uncompromising with rioters, looters and all those who commit acts of violence," Nunez told reporters on Friday after meetings involving President Emmanuel Macron, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu and senior security officials.

Nunez said authorities had identified numerous online calls from hard-left groups encouraging attacks and urging activists to target public buildings.

"We are not talking about a nice, friendly demonstration," Nunez said, adding: "We are ready for tomorrow. We will be extremely vigilant, extremely firm, and we will let absolutely nothing pass."

Museums, Major Events Shuttered as Precaution

Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the streets of France in recent weeks, but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have taken advantage of the dispute to sow chaos.

Police have authorised only a union demonstration in Paris on Saturday, rejecting requests for rallies lodged by France's main student union, UNEF, and the Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that first emerged in 2018.

Many French cities beyond Paris have also banned protests, including France's second and third largest cities, Marseille and Lyon.

UNEF said its rallies, which grew from high school protests last month against teacher shortages and shabby facilities, would go ahead regardless.

Fears of renewed turmoil prompted several of Paris' best-known cultural institutions, including the Louvre, to close on Saturday, while the city's normally bustling Art Basel fair will remain shut throughout the weekend.

Business groups also urged shops to stay shut after some 3,000 stores and businesses were ransacked last weekend.

Nunez said 10,000 more police would be on the streets than a week ago, while the specialist RAID and GIGN units, mounted police, helicopters, drones and anti-drone systems would be deployed across the country.

Armoured vehicles and water cannon vehicles would also be available, while curfews imposed in some sensitive areas this past week would remain in force.

Far-Right Congress a Possible Flashpoint

Authorities are also concerned that the annual congress of Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally in Orleans this weekend could become a flashpoint, with left-wing and anti-racist groups announcing counter-demonstrations.

The upsurge of violence has boosted poll ratings for Le Pen, who is the frontrunner for next year's presidential election. She has portrayed the unrest as evidence of a collapse in state authority.

Adding to tensions, one person was killed and four injured in a shooting west of Paris on Friday in an attack that police said could be racially motivated.

Macron is due to meet student representatives later on Friday for the first time, seeking to de-escalate a crisis that has exposed deep social and political tensions.

Marylise Leon, the general secretary of the CFDT, one of the nation's largest trade unions, criticised him on Friday for refusing to grant permission to more rallies on Saturday.

"It's counterproductive because there is a lot of anger, a lot of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to," she told French broadcaster TF1. "It's not for the president to decide who can legitimately request to protest."

The social turbulence has intensified scrutiny of France's economic outlook and ratings agency Moody's is widely expected to cut the French credit rating on Friday, underscoring concern that the government had not reined in public spending.

item.title: Shops, malls to close at 8pm
item.media:keywords: shops, opening hours, malls, markets, Durga Puja
item.description: On Oct 5, the Power Division extended the opening hours of shops by two hours to 10pm for the Puja holiday
item.content:encoded:
The government has decided not to extend the special consideration that allowed keeping shopping malls, markets and shops in Dhaka open until 10pm for Durga Puja.

Accordingly, shopping malls, markets and shops will once again close after 8pm from Friday, as per their regular schedule.

On Oct 5, the Power Division extended the opening hours of shops by two hours to 10pm for the Puja holiday.

The shops are usually open from 11am to 8pm.

The government has adjusted the opening hours of shops several times this year as part of power conservation and energy management.

item.title: ‘Sniper’ comment lands man in jail
item.media:keywords: Jail, detention, Anti-Terrorism Act, Sniper, facebook, comment, Tarique Rahman
item.description: The case investigating officer says law enforcers will later petition the court for him to be interrogated in police custody
item.content:encoded:
Abu Bokor Siddique, who was arrested in Rajshahi for commenting on a Facebook post suggesting a sniper could have targeted a bus carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, has been sent to jail in a case under the Anti-Terrorism Act.

Case investigating officer Sub-Inspector (SI) Yasin Paik of the Cyber and Special Crime Division of the police’s Detective Branch presented the accused in court and requested he be detained in jail.

In response, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mehedi Hasan ordered that he be sent to jail, said SI Shah Alam of the Prosecution Division.

The Special Response Battalion (SRB) had arrested Abu Bokor from his house in the Kochuatoil area of Paba Thana in Rajshahi late on Wednesday night. Later, DB police officially arrested him under the Anti-Terrorism Act.

Tarique visited Rajshahi on Tuesday. After landing at Shah Makhdum Airport, he entered the city in a bus from the Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology (RUET).

Crowds lined both sides of the road to greet him, and he waved back from the moving bus.

A Facebook page called “The Beauty of Rajshahi” later posted a photo of the bus, questioning why a RUET vehicle was used instead of the red-and-green bulletproof bus meant for the prime minister.

An account under the name “MD Abu Bokor Siddique” commented on the post: “What a golden chance. All that was missing was a sniper.”

The comment spread across social media and drew broad debate.

SI Manik Hossain of the Cyber and Special Crime (North) Division of the DB filed a case under the Anti-Terrorism Act at Ramna Police Station in the capital over the incident.

Law enforcers will later petition the court for the detainee to be interrogated in police custody, said SI Yasin in his plea to detain Abu Bokor in jail.

item.title: 7 patients with measles symptoms die
item.media:keywords: Measles, Deaths, hospitalisations, Health, Disease
item.description: The latest deaths include three in Sylhet and two in Dhaka
item.content:encoded:
At least seven people with symptoms of measles have died across Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The latest deaths have taken the number of recorded deaths among people with measles symptoms to 1,110 this year.

Another 104 people have died after testing positive for measles, taking the overall death toll from the disease and its symptoms to 1,214.

The DGHS said in its bulletin on Thursday that three of the deaths were reported in the Sylhet Division, two in the Dhaka Division, and one each in the Chattogram and Mymensingh divisions.

Dhaka has recorded the highest number of deaths among patients with measles symptoms, at 498.

Sylhet follows with 197 deaths, while Chattogram has reported 103, Rajshahi 93, Mymensingh 86, Barishal 65, Khulna 51 and Rangpur 17.

According to the bulletin, another 1,110 people with measles symptoms sought treatment at hospitals across the country in the past 24 hours. Of them, 1,025 were admitted to hospital. Measles was confirmed in 25 people during the period.

Among the newly admitted patients with measles symptoms, 456 were in Dhaka Division, 189 in Chattogram, 94 in Sylhet, 115 in Barishal, 60 in Khulna, 65 in Mymensingh, 22 in Rajshahi and 24 in Rangpur.

The bulletin said the total number of hospital admissions has reached 194,633, of whom 186,798 have recovered and returned home.

Meanwhile, the number of people reported with measles symptoms has risen to 218,870. Of them, 23,273 have tested positive for measles.

The health directorate has been keeping records of measles cases, suspected cases and deaths since Mar 15.

Not all patients who seek hospital treatment, or those who remain outside hospitals, are tested for measles. As a result, the exact number of confirmed measles cases is not available. Only data on patients who visit or are admitted to hospitals are recorded.

item.title: Drive-by shooting near Paris leaves one dead
item.media:keywords: France, Shooting, Trappes, Paris, Crime, Police, Investigation
item.description: A suspect has been arrested after a gunman opened fire from a car in Trappes
item.content:encoded:
One person was killed and at least four others were injured in a shooting in the Yvelines district west of Paris, and a suspect has been arrested, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Friday.

Ali Rabeh, the mayor of the Yvelines town of Trappes, told BFMTV that a man had fired shoots from his car and "appeared to be firing at random and seemed intent on carrying out a massacre".

He said one of those injured was a 12-year-old girl, adding that the shooter lived in a near-by town. There was no information so far about his motives, he said.

Lecornu wrote on X that security forces had been fully mobilised. "The national anti-terrorism prosecutor’s office has announced that it is monitoring the situation," he added.

Representatives for the prosecutor's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and the prefecture declined to comment. The anti-terrorism prosecutor's office confirmed it was monitoring the case.

item.title: 3 die of dengue, 1,299 more hospitalised
item.media:keywords: Dengue, Deaths, hospitalisations, Health, Disease
item.description: Deaths from the Aedes mosquito-borne disease rise in October
item.content:encoded:
Bangladesh has recorded three more dengue deaths in a 24-hour count while 1,299 others have been admitted to hospitals around the country.

The latest deaths bring this year’s toll from the mosquito-borne disease to 371, the Directorate General of Health Services said on Friday.

Another 1,296 patients left hospitals after recovery, the bulletin said. So far this year, the number of patients hospitalised with dengue has hit 119,801. Of them, 113,409 have been released after recovery.

Among the latest fatalities reported, one occurred at a hospital in the Chattogram Division and one in the Mymensingh Division, according to the health directorate.

Of the new admissions, 116 were in Dhaka North City Corporation and 131 in Dhaka South.

Another 274 were admitted to hospitals elsewhere in Dhaka Division.

Elsewhere, Barishal Division recorded 159 admissions, Chattogram 219, Khulna 147, Mymensingh 100, Rajshahi 113, Rangpur 38 and Sylhet one.

The DGHS has recorded dengue hospitalisations and deaths since 2000. The worst year was 2023, when 321,179 people were hospitalised and 1,705 died from the disease.

Last year, dengue killed more than 400 people, while around 102,000 cases were identified.

October has accounted for 123 deaths in the first 21 days of this year.

item.title: 4 of a family burnt in Gazipur fire
item.media:keywords: burns, family , Gazipur, Fire
item.description: Two of them have been admitted to the hospital
item.content:encoded:
Four members of a family, including two children, have suffered burns in a fire at a house in Gazipur’s Sadar Upazila.

The injured were taken to the National Burn and Plastic Surgery Institute on Friday morning after the incident occurred around dawn.

The victims have been identified as Molsin Prodhan, 30, his wife Selina Akhter, 25, and their children Sohad, 4, and Shayan, 5.

Members of the family saw that a sofa in the house was on fire around dawn. The flames then spread to the wooden roof and two motorcycles that were parked on the verandah. The blaze eventually spread to the rest of the house.

The cause and source of the fire have yet to be confirmed.

The injured were first taken to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital. From there, they were sent to the burn institute for advanced treatment.

Sultan Mahmud Sikder, resident doctor at the institute’s emergency division, said that Selina had suffered burns on 40 percent of her body, Shayan on 12 percent, Sohad on 2 percent and Molsin on 1 percent.

The mother and older brother of the family have been admitted to the burn institute, while the father and the younger brother are under observation.

item.title: Saudi plant expansion may produce stronger missiles: study
item.media:keywords: Saudi Arabia, ballistic missiles, missile production, China, Iran, China ambassador, Air China, Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia relations
item.description: Satellite images show new buildings at a complex near Riyadh, with researchers saying the facility could be ready to produce missiles by the end of the year
item.content:encoded:
Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two US researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images.

More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia to deter attacks by Iran and make its military more self-reliant, while possibly strengthening its position in a deadly conflict with Yemen's Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.

But they risk fueling a regional missile race and could deepen opposition in the US Congress to a US-Saudi civilian nuclear agreement that has already raised concerns about proliferation.

Satellite company Planet Labs, based in the US, took images of the al-Duwadimi complex about 125 miles (200km) west of Riyadh between April 2025 and September 2026.

The two researchers, Sam Lair and Michael Duitsman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute, assessed that those images show a new building that houses casting pits -- wells in which a mixture of fuel ingredients is poured into missile motor casings and allowed to harden.

The Saudi embassy and Information Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

The building, flanked by what appear to be walls to protect nearby structures from accidental explosions, is at least twice as large as the one believed to house the plant’s existing casting pits, Lair and Duitsman said in their assessment. The Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) is a non-partisan research organization in Philadelphia.

A second new building could be used to store fuel ingredients or finished missile components, they said.

The imagery "suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges," they wrote.

Militaries favor solid-fuel missiles because they can be stored for long periods and launched more quickly than liquid-fuel systems.

Lair and Duitsman and experts from the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) and the CNA research and analysis organization told Reuters that the makeup of Saudi Arabia's missile force suggests that the al-Duwadimi complex relies on Chinese technology. Lair and Duitsman said that its characteristics also are similar to Chinese missile plants.

Saudi Arabia secretly acquired about 40 liquid-fuel DF-3 ballistic missiles from China in 1987, according to a 1991 declassified CIA estimate. It displayed two of them for the first time in an April 2014 military parade, according to a Youtube video and photographs of the event.

The FPRI team also recently identified from social media videos and photos what they assessed was the wreckage in Yemen of a Saudi-fired Chinese-designed DF-15 missile.

Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile.

Riyadh is believed to have turned to Beijing because Washington has long restricted exports of longer-range missile systems.

The Chinese embassy and defense ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The CIA declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

Missiles Would Alter the Balance of Power

Sascha Bruchmann, a research fellow at IISS, said longer-range missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to strike Iran without risking its US-supplied F-15 jet fighters against Iranian air defenses.

“You’d want a system to threaten whatever is holy to Tehran ... if you don’t have the political will to send an F-15 with JDAMs over Tehran,” said Bruchmann, referring to US-made satellite-guided bombs. “Iran has a lead because its missiles and drones can strike Saudi wherever it wants. The Saudis could close that capability gap a bit.”

Bruchmann, who reviewed the FPRI analysis at Reuters request, concurred that the expansion of al-Duwadimi could be for producing more powerful solid-fuel missiles.

Janes, the defense intelligence company, also reviewed it and said the buildings “may suggest an effort to expand production capability or support the development of longer-range missiles.”

Saudi Arabia's apparent pursuit of more powerful missiles comes as other Gulf powers are also seeking to expand their offensive and defensive arsenals, said Decker Eveleth, a CNA analyst who has been tracking the al-Duwadimi construction with commercial satellite imagery and concurred with the FPRI assessment.

“This is being replicated across the Middle East,” he said. “You see exactly the same thing happening in the UAE. You see the exact same thing happening in Turkey. Everybody is doing this now.”

The expansion of al-Duwadimi could have political consequences in the US by stiffening bipartisan congressional opposition to a US-Saudi agreement under which the US would help Riyadh establish uranium enrichment for power generation.

Opponents say that the deal lacks sufficient safeguards to prevent Riyadh from secretly building a nuclear weapon. The kingdom has denied any such plan.

Work Began Last Year

The FPRI assessment said the Planet Labs imagery showed that the expansion at al-Duwadimi began in April 2025 with ground-clearing and digging for the suspected storage building. Work on the suspected casting-pit building began later that month or in early May, it said.

A Dec 12, 2025, photo showed what researchers assessed were two deep pits inside the building that had no roof yet.

A Sept 18, 2026, photo shows the roof still partly missing and "heavy duty blast diverting walls" on either side to prevent accidental explosions from damaging adjacent structures.

The walls, the researchers said, are somewhat similar to those depicted in imagery of US and Iranian missile plants and "further evidence the building is for casting solid propellant motors."

Finishing the roofs would not take long, the FPRI said, but installing casting equipment may take several months. The facility could be ready to start producing missiles as early as the end of the year.

item.title: Winter chill likely from early November
item.media:keywords: weather forecast, Winter, BMD, Met Office
item.description: Temperatures have begun already to dip in northern districts, with cooler weather expected nationwide
item.content:encoded:
A hint of winter is in the air in northern Bangladesh, with temperatures expected to fall further across the country from the first week of November.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department forecast the change on Friday, as temperatures in several northern districts began to dip, meteorologist Tariful Newaz Kabir told bdnews24.com.

Tetulia has recorded day and night temperatures below 20 degrees Celsius, while readings in Rajarhat and Dinajpur have ranged between 20 and 21 degrees. Temperatures have also fallen in Rajshahi and Ishurdi.

“Once the current weather system passes next week, temperatures may fall a little more,” the meteorologist said.

“From the first week of November, they are likely to drop further. Then the winter feel may grow across the country, Dhaka included.”

A low-pressure system, meanwhile, has formed over the east-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal, with the system likely to intensify.

It could develop into a depression on Saturday and later strengthen into a deep depression, Kabir said.

The system has yet to affect Bangladesh, but coastal areas could see some rain after Oct 25.

Rain is unlikely elsewhere over the next 24 to 48 hours, with dry conditions expected to prevail across the country, the meteorologist said.

item.title: Gold cheaper for third time in 10 days
item.media:keywords: global market, Bangladesh, silver price, BAJUS, Gold price
item.description: The price of 22-carat gold falls by Tk 2,158 a Bhori to Tk 224,182, while silver prices also decline
item.content:encoded:
Gold prices have fallen for the third time in 10 days, with the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) cutting the price of 22-carat gold by Tk 2,158 to Tk 224,182 a Bhori.

The new rates took effect nationwide at 10am on Friday, with prices of other gold grades and silver also reduced.

The latest cut brings the total decline in 22-carat gold prices to Tk 7,115 a Bhori over 10 days.

Dewan Aminul Islam Shaheen, chairman of the BAJUS Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring, attributed the reductions to falling international prices.

“The local gold market depends entirely on the global market. When international prices rise, we adjust and set prices accordingly. When they fall, we cut,” he told bdnews24.com.

“The international market is now on a downward path, falling by the moment. We are cutting prices in the local market in line with it.”

On Thursday, BAJUS cut the price of 22-carat gold by Tk 1,691 a Bhori. It had previously reduced the price by Tk 3,266 on Oct 13, following an increase of Tk 2,216 on Oct 9.

Under the new rates, hallmarked 22-carat gold costs Tk 19,220 a gram, including VAT. With one Bhori equivalent to 11.664g, the price comes to approximately Tk 224,182.

A Bhori of 21-carat gold now costs Tk 214,093, while 18-carat gold is priced at Tk 183,883 and traditional-method gold at Tk 150,232.

Before the latest adjustment, 22-carat gold cost Tk 226,340 a Bhori, 21-carat Tk 216,192, 18-carat Tk 185,691 and traditional-method gold Tk 151,690.

The reductions amount to Tk 2,099 for 21-carat gold, Tk 1,808 for 18-carat gold and Tk 1,458 for traditional-method gold.

In a statement, BAJUS said the price of Tejabi (pure) gold had fallen in the local market, prompting the latest adjustment after a review of overall market conditions.

Global Market Also Down

Gold crossed $5,500 an ounce on Jan 29, reaching $5,511.28 before climbing above $5,600 later.

Prices have fluctuated since then.

At 1pm Bangladesh time on Friday, spot gold was trading at $4,012.41 an ounce, down from $4,098.74 on Thursday, when domestic prices were also reduced.

Reuters reported on Thursday that gold prices had fallen amid concerns over rising oil prices and inflation.

Silver Prices

BAJUS has also lowered silver prices.

Hallmarked 22-carat silver now costs Tk 330 a gram, or Tk 3,849 a Bhori, down Tk 175 from Tk 4,024.

Prices of other silver grades have also been reduced.

item.title: How China's Communist Party plenum works
item.media:keywords: China, Beijing, Communist Party, plenum, central committee, Xi Jinping
item.description: The meeting is the fifth time the roughly 300 full and alternate members of China's Central Committee have gathered since 2022
item.content:encoded:
The elite Central Committee of China's ruling Communist Party holds a closed-door meeting in Beijing from Monday to Thursday that will set the political tone ahead of late 2027's once-every-five years party congress, and potentially discuss key personnel moves.

Here are some key facts about the plenum and how it works.

The meeting is the fifth time the roughly 300 full and alternate members of China's Central Committee — the largest of the party's top decision-making bodies — have gathered since 2022's congress confirmed top leader Xi Jinping's norm-breaking third term in office.

While the official theme is tightening discipline in the party's ranks, key personnel deliberations and what to do about disgraced former officials are also likely to feature prominently.

To prevent leaks, plenum attendees are traditionally confined to the venue for the duration of the meeting.

Little, if any, news of the proceedings is made public until it closes. Foreign media and most Chinese reporters are given no access

On the day the plenum closes, the official Xinhua news agency is expected to issue a dispatch, giving details of what was agreed, albeit typically full of opaque party terminology.

To portray party unity, there will almost certainly be no mention of any disagreements within the senior leadership.

A more detailed document will usually follow several days later

Past plenums have been held under tight security at the Soviet-era Jingxi Hotel in western Beijing. The location of this year's meeting has not been announced.

The mood at plenums can vary greatly, depending on the agenda. A watershed conclave in 1978 overseen by Deng Xiaoping kick-started China's economic reforms, beginning the transformation of the country from a centrally planned backwater to an economic powerhouse.

item.title: 7,500 Bangladeshis in Saudi prisons: Shama
item.media:keywords: Saudi Arabia, Shama Obaed Islam, foreign ministry, migrant workers, Saudi executions
item.description: Shama Obaed says Dhaka has sought details over the execution of two Bangladeshis in Makkah, saying Saudi authorities did not inform it beforehand
item.content:encoded:
Around 7,500 Bangladeshis are being held in prisons across Saudi Arabia on various charges, according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam.

She disclosed the figure on Friday while speaking to reporters after the body of Shahed Ahmed, a Bangladeshi killed in Saudi Arabia, was brought back to Dhaka.

"According to Bangladesh government records, around 7,500 expatriate Bangladeshis are currently held in prisons in different cities across Saudi Arabia," she said.

Shama added that Saudi authorities periodically sent lists of Bangladeshis convicted of various offences.

She also said Bangladesh had yet to receive details about the execution of two nationals, Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akter, on Oct 14 over allegations of "immoral acts" at a mosque in Makkah.

Bangladesh was not informed before the executions, according to Shama.

The Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah has written to Saudi authorities seeking information, while the matter has also been raised with the Saudi ambassador in Dhaka.

"We have officially written to the Saudi government requesting copies of the verdicts. Once we receive them, we will be able to learn the details of what happened," Shama said.

She acknowledged Saudi Arabia's right to enforce its own laws but stressed that Bangladesh should be informed when its nationals face such punishment.

The state minister also questioned whether the previous Awami League government and the interim administration had done enough, noting that the alleged incident dated back to 2023.

She urged patience as Bangladesh pursued the matter through diplomatic channels.

Shama said the government was also seeking visa extensions for Bangladeshis stranded at home because of the conflict in West Asia and would explore support for expatriates who had lost their jobs.

item.title: Dipu Moni taken to DMCH for check-up
item.media:keywords: Dhaka Medical College Hospital, Dhaka Central Jail, Dipu Moni, Moni
item.description: She has been in jail since her arrest in August 2024
item.content:encoded:
Former minister and Awami League leader Dipu Moni has undergone a health check-up at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) after being brought from Dhaka Central Jail.

A team from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of police took the former MP to the hospital around 11:45am on Friday.

After a medical check-up and preliminary tests, she was returned to jail under police guard around 12:15pm, CID Police Inspector Md Redwan said.
