Police arrested her in Dhaka’s Baridhara on Aug 19, 2024, after the fall of the Awami League government in that year’s student-led mass uprising. She has been in jail since.

The Awami League joint general secretary is accused in about 70 cases, including crimes against humanity, corruption and violence during the July Uprising.

Her husband Tawfique Nawaz, a prominent Supreme Court lawyer, died on Aug 18 while she was in jail.

Dipu Moni was released on parole to attend his funeral.

item.title: All 14 Indians 'safe' after Yemen coast yacht incident
item.media:keywords: Red Sea, maritime security, Houthis, Yemen, India
item.description: The Indian Embassy says it remains in touch with the nationals to ensure their safety
item.content:encoded:
All 14 Indian nationals on a yacht involved in an incident off Yemen's coast are reported safe, the Indian embassy in Yemen said on Friday.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Thursday they were rescuing a boat carrying 14 Indians that was attacked off Jabal Zuqar island near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and blamed Saudi Arabia for the attack.

Saudi authorities did not respond to a Reuters request for comment on Thursday.

"Reports suggest that all 14 Indian nationals are safe and located around Hodeidah in Yemen. We will continue to work to ensure their well-being," the Indian embassy in Yemen said in a post on X, without elaborating.

The embassy earlier said that precise information on the 14 Indians was not available and that they were making attempts to establish the circumstances and facts of the incident.

India is the world's third-largest supplier of seafarers, with more than 300,000 sailors working across global shipping fleets, according to government data.

More than a dozen Indian seafarers have been killed, and three are missing in the Gulf and the wider West Asian maritime region since the Middle East conflict began in February.

Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognised government have raged since the group pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth.

India's foreign ministry said on Thursday that it condemned the attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, terming them "unacceptable."

item.title: Shreya Ghoshal reveals why she re-recorded ‘Sun Raha Hai Na Tu’
item.media:keywords: Aashiqui 2, Shraddha Kapoor, Shreya Ghoshal, Bollywood, Entertainment
item.description: The singer shares the behind-the-scenes story of how the popular “Aashiqui 2” track took shape after an unexpected request from the filmmakers
item.content:encoded:
Shreya Ghoshal has revealed that she had to re-record “Sun Raha Hai Na Tu” for "Aashiqui 2" after director Mohit Suri and producer Mukesh Bhatt asked her to simplify her rendition to suit Shraddha Kapoor’s character.

The 2013 romantic musical featured Shraddha as Aarohi, an aspiring singer who is discovered by Aditya Roy Kapur’s character Rahul while performing at a bar.

Speaking to Billboard India, Shreya said she had not seen Shraddha when she first recorded the song but knew that the character was not yet a professional singer.

“Shraddha was very new. I did not know how she looked. But I think the context of knowing that she is not yet a professional singer... she is just singing in a club or a bar somewhere, where she gets noticed by the actor Aditya Roy Kapur. So she is yet to become the singer that she will eventually become. So keeping it simple was very essential,” she said.

Shreya said her first recording reflected her own interpretation of the song and included the vocal embellishments she would naturally use as a trained singer.

She later received a call from Suri and Bhatt, who explained that Aarohi was supposed to be an inexperienced singer at that point in the story.

“This girl has yet to learn how to sing. She’s very new. So you listen to it (the song) once again. If you feel like, you can record it again,” she recalled them telling her.

Shreya then recorded the track again, removing some of the flourishes and keeping the notes straightforward to better reflect the character.

She said the director had not been present in the studio during her first recording, and their subsequent conversation helped her understand why a different approach was needed.

Shreya added that she performs “Sun Raha Hai Na Tu” differently at concerts, where she can bring a more polished and technically elaborate style to the song.

For playback singing, however, she said understanding the story and the character is crucial, as factors such as age, background and musical training can shape how a song should be performed.

item.title: Apple enters foldable market with iPhone Duo launch
item.media:keywords: Apple, iPhone Duo, foldable phone, smartphone, John Ternus
item.description: Demand outpaced supply within minutes of pre-orders opening, with delivery dates slipping to late January and Apple capping orders at two per customer
item.content:encoded:
Sales of Apple's first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, began on Friday, with market watchers betting on whether the device can reinvent the small foldables market in the same way the iPhone did for smartphones.

The Duo's reception could prove an early test for new CEO John Ternus, the former hardware chief who unveiled the phone barely a week after taking charge in September.

It could also have large implications for a niche category in which rivals such as Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold premium offerings for several years.

Within minutes of pre-orders opening last Friday, Apple's estimated delivery dates for the Duo had slipped to late January as demand outpaced supply. The US company called the response from customers "nothing short of extraordinary."

With the massive demand, Apple capped pre-orders at two handsets per customer and limited sales significantly for walk-in shoppers, resulting in muted crowds unlike the hype that typically accompanied new iPhone releases.

In China, France, Hong Kong, India and Japan, units would be available only for customers who had ordered online

In Sydney, the first Apple store to sell the phones on Friday, a queue of customers formed outside before opening at 8am local time (2100 GMT).

Simon Krishnan, a 48-year-old engineer, paid A$ 3,899(2,734) for a Duo with 512GB memory.

"This is a bit of a luxury item for me, because it's so expensive, but I just think, you know what? Life's too short," he said.

In China, a soft consumer market combined with memory costs pushing prices higher has led to six straight quarters of declines in smartphone shipments. Apple's market share, however, has rebounded as some phone buyers trade up to premium devices while others seek value at the lower end of the market, putting pressure on mid-range brands.

Liu Wei, a 26-year-old healthcare professional, already has a foldable phone from Xiaomi, but still queued outside a central Shanghai Apple store from 6 am to get his hands on Apple's first foldable.

"I've used Apple products for many years, and I have more trust (in the brand), so I bought one on launch day to try it out," he said.

In Hong Kong, May, 38, who declined to give his full name for privacy reasons, secured a 256GB iPhone Duo, which retails for HK$ 17,499 (2,231.73), during an online pre‑sale and aimed to resell the handset for a profit of around HK$4,000: “A few meals' worth of money,” he joked.

MIXED REVIEWS

Early reviews have praised the Duo's design as well as its sturdy and barely visible hinge, a major feat for phones whose prominent creased screen has long been a drawback and potential deterrent for buyers.

But reviewers have said camera compromises, including the absence of a telephoto lens and third-party apps that still need to be reworked for the new display size, could disappoint some buyers.

They have also said the Duo in its smaller, folded state is less handy for the litany of quick tasks that most users carry out each day on standard iPhones, with several prominent reviewers recommending against the Duo for many Apple customers.

"It's been a lot of fun trying the Duo out for a week, but it feels like I've gotten to use an extraordinarily polished prototype -- not a finished product that I'd want to buy and carry," longtime Apple commentator John Gruber, author of the blog Daring Fireball, wrote in a review.

Tech commentator Marques Brownlee, popularly known as MKBHD, said in a YouTube review that "if you're just a regular person who doesn't do much more than texting, social media and browsing here and there, then it is probably a no. But if the $2,000 doesn't mean much to you, and you like the idea, after the learning curve and getting used to not having facial identification, it is a really fun phone."

TOUGH TO FIND

The limited supplies could disappoint Apple fans lining up in front of stores to buy the Duo. Apple told Reuters that walk-in availability would vary by country, with limited stocks in the US, Australia, Canada, Mexico and much of Britain and Europe.

"Foldables have been an established category for years, but adoption has remained relatively limited compared with conventional smartphones. Apple's entry could bring the format to a much broader audience," said Francisco Jeronimo, vice president at market research firm IDC.

IDC expects Apple will take 44 percent of the foldable value in 2026 on 31 percent of foldable units. By 2027, it will become the market leader in the category both in value and units shipped, IDC forecasts.

"Apple has made a convincing case for this form factor," Jeronimo said after spending a week with the passport-shaped Duo.

"Now comes the next test: turning excitement into availability, adoption and a lasting new chapter for the smartphone market," Jeronimo said.

item.title: President visits ailing Moyeen Khan at hospital
item.media:keywords: Abdul Moyeen Khan, Mirza Fakhrul, Evercare Hospital, local government minister, President

item.content:encoded:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has visited Local Government Minister Abdul Moyeen Khan, who is undergoing treatment at a hospital.

Bangabhaban, which serves as the president’s official residence and office, confirmed the visit to Evercare Hospital on Friday morning.

He asked after the minister and wished him a speedy recovery, it said. The minister’s wife, lawyer Roksana Khandaker, was present. item.title: Tiger Shroff's mother to pay injured vlogger's medical bills
item.media:keywords: Tiger Shroff, Ayesha Shroff, Umesh Chauhan, Mumbai shooting, Bollywood, Indian cinema, medical expenses, Juhu shooting
item.description: A stray bullet struck Umesh Chauhan in the chest when gunmen opened fire at the Bollywood actor’s BMW in Mumbai
item.content:encoded:
Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff's mother Ayesha Shroff has offered to cover the medical bills of a vlogger wounded when gunmen opened fire on the actor's car in Mumbai.

Umesh Chauhan, a vlogger and a fan of Tiger, was standing outside a football ground near Pushpa Park in Juhu when the attackers fired at the actor's BMW, The Indian Express reports.

A stray bullet struck Chauhan in the lower left side of his chest.

He was initially taken to Cooper Hospital before being transferred to KEM Hospital, where doctors removed a 1.5cm bullet during surgery on Oct 21.

Chauhan's cousin Rahul Goud told Mid-Day that Ayesha had provided financial assistance and promised to cover his remaining treatment costs.

“Ayesha madam gave me some money yesterday, and some amount was given to me today. She assured me that they will take care of the entire treatment cost and post-surgery medical requirements,” he said.

Chauhan's father expressed gratitude for the support and said the family was relieved that his son was responding well to treatment.

“We are thankful for the help and feel relieved after his bullet was removed and seeing him respond well to the treatment. We hope he recovers completely now so that he can take care of his wife and expected child,” he said.

Ayesha had earlier briefly spoken to reporters and, giving a thumbs-up, said: “God is kind.”

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, who visited Tiger following the shooting, said the incident had left the actor and his mother shaken.

He also said strict action would be taken against those responsible for the attack.

The Shooting

Tiger was leaving a football stadium in Mumbai after a game when two assailants allegedly fired seven rounds at his car.

Five bullets struck the vehicle, injuring his driver and at least one other person.

After the shooting, the two gunmen fled on a motorcycle allegedly kept ready by a third accomplice.

Tiger then took the wheel and drove his injured driver to Nanavati Hospital.

item.title: Kareena-Shahid hug at IIFA sparks ‘Jab We Met 2’ calls
item.media:keywords: Indian Cinema, Kareena Kapoor Khan, Shahid Kapoor, hug, Jab We Met, fans, Reunion
item.description: The former couple’s interaction rekindles memories of Geet and Aditya in the movie Jab We Met, prompting fans to call for an on-screen reunion
item.content:encoded:
Kareena Kapoor and Shahid Kapoor have sent fans on a nostalgia trip after the former couple shared a hug at an IIFA 2027 press conference in Mumbai.

Their cordial exchange at Thursday’s event brought back memories of their 2007 romantic comedy “Jab We Met”, with fans taking to social media to call for the actors to reunite as Geet and Aditya in a sequel.

Kareena, dressed in a black leather top and skirt, and Shahid, wearing a white suit, were seen greeting each other warmly at the event, Indian broadcaster NDTV reports.

Videos of the encounter quickly circulated on social media, drawing emotional reactions from fans who still cherish their chemistry in the Imtiaz Ali-directed film.

“Why am I getting emotional seeing this?” one social media user wrote, while another asked: “Why are we so happy?”

“We get emotional,” another fan wrote, while one simply commented: “Geet and Aditya.”

Others called for an on-screen reunion.

“My Roman Empire,” one user wrote, while another said: “We want jab we met reunion.”

Some fans also linked the encounter to the so-called “October theory”, a social media trend suggesting that the month brings either a new person into someone’s life or a reunion with an ex.

“Guys, October theory is real,” one user wrote.

“Geet and Aditya in parallel universe,” another said.

It was not the first time an encounter between Kareena and Shahid at an IIFA event had drawn attention.

In March 2025, the two greeted each other with a hug at an IIFA press conference in Jaipur.

Shahid later played down the attention surrounding the meeting, saying such encounters were normal for them.

“For us, it’s nothing new... today we met on the stage and we keep on meeting here and there, but it’s totally normal for us... if people felt nice, it’s nice,” he said.

Kareena and Shahid were among Bollywood’s most talked-about couples before their relationship ended in 2007, around the time Jab We Met was being filmed.

The romantic comedy, which also featured Tarun Arora, became one of the most popular films of their careers, with Kareena’s Geet and Shahid’s Aditya remaining fan favourites nearly two decades later.

Both actors have since married and started families.

Kareena married actor Saif Ali Khan in 2012. They have two sons, Taimur and Jeh.

Shahid married Mira Rajput on Jul 7, 2015. They have two children, daughter Misha and son Zain.

Mira and Kareena also recently drew attention after Mira appeared on Kareena’s talk show What Women Want.

After the shoot, Mira shared photographs from the set and wrote: “What women want is to be themselves. Thanks @kareenakapoorkhan for having me and for being the woman you are.”

Kareena responded: “So happy you came, gorgeous.”

She also posted a photograph with Mira on Instagram Stories, describing her as “the absolutely warm and lovely Mira”.

Mira reshared the post, writing: “Could not have better company. With the gorgeous Kareena Kapoor Khan.”

item.title: Patwary, Hasnat move up NCP ranks
item.media:keywords: Politics, NCP, leadership reshuffle, Nasiruddin Patwary, Hasnat Abdullah, Sarjis Alam, Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, Nahid Islam
item.description: Nahid Islam and Akhter Hossen retain their top posts as the party reorganises its leadership nearly two years after its formation
item.content:encoded:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has reshuffled its top brass, promoting Nasiruddin Patwary and Hasnat Abdullah while placing Sarjis Alam and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain in lower-ranking positions.

The party, formed by student leaders of the 2024 mass uprising, announced the changes in a Facebook post on Friday.

The reshuffle comes nearly two years after the NCP's formation, with the party yet to hold a national council.

Nahid Islam remains convenor, while Akhter Hossen retains his post as member secretary.

Patwary and Hasnat have been named senior joint convenors.

Hasnat previously served as chief organiser for the southern region, while Patwary was chief coordinator.

Sarjis, formerly chief organiser for the northern region, and Asif, the party's spokesperson, have been appointed senior joint member secretaries.

The new positions place them below Patwary and Hasnat in the leadership hierarchy.

Samantha Sharmin has also been moved from senior joint convenor to joint convenor.

A prominent NCP leader since the July Uprising, she did not contest the Feb 12 parliamentary election because of the party's alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami.

item.title: Netflix, Hoichoi team up for Bengali series
item.media:keywords: Netflix, Hoichoi, Bengali series, Bohemian Ghora, Mohanagar, 22nd president of Bangladesh
item.description: Director Amitabh Reza celebrates global expansion as Bangladeshi hit “Bohemian Ghora” crosses borders
item.content:encoded:
Bengali storytelling is about to find a far bigger stage as Netflix and Hoichoi have struck a two-year partnership that will carry every series the Bengali streamer launches to Hindi, Tamil and Telugu audiences.

The two companies unveiled the deal in Mumbai on Thursday, according to Variety.

The dubbed versions will stream exclusively on Netflix, arriving in all three languages on the same day as each Bengali debut on Hoichoi, the digital news platform said.

The first out of the gate is “The Cursed Temple of Kauriburi”, a horror series steeped in folklore that premieres on Nov 6, with Jeetu Kamal, Solanki Roy and Paoli Dam in the leads.

More releases will follow over the coming months.

Netflix will also carry 14 existing Hoichoi series: "Madam Inspector", "Sampurna", "Lajja", "Eken Sirji", "Anjaan Saaye", "The Curse of Parnashavari", "Bloodlines", "The Adventures of Daadi & Jagga", "Raat Abhi Baaki Hain", "Achinta: Trial By Law", "Shaadi Ka Siyappa", "Queens", "Parineeta: A Love Story" and "Mahanagar".

The slate ranges from crime thrillers and detective mysteries to folklore horror, social and courtroom drama, and romance.

The partners will also create new shows together.

Netflix and Hoichoi will develop original series that reimagine selected Hoichoi stories, with Hoichoi Studios producing.

The companies said each adaptation would bring in fresh creative voices. Further details have yet to be revealed.

The news has already stirred excitement in Bangladesh. “Bohemian Ghora” director Amitabh Reza Chowdhury marked the moment in a Facebook post on Thursday.

“‘Bohemian Ghora’ is not just the story of a truck driver’s eight wives. It is a story of Bangladesh’s soil, its people, its folk culture, the tangles of relationships and life’s many odd shades of humour,” he wrote.

“There is laughter, love and deceit, and there are the strange tricks people use to survive.

“This story, scattered along the roads of Bangladesh, is now reaching an international audience.

“From Hoichoi to Netflix — Bohemian Ghora continues its journey beyond borders!

“Bangladesh’s stories, Bangladesh’s people, Bangladesh’s own sense of humour, now before the world.”

For Netflix, the pact is part of a wider drive to bolster its originals with more licensed programming from outside producers.

The streamer said its global audience, which it puts at close to a billion people, gives studios, networks and creators a compelling reason to work with it, the digital news platform reports.

The Hoichoi deal follows two other high-profile licensing moves. In France, Netflix now carries the full programming lineup of broadcaster TF1.

In Brazil, it struck a deal earlier this month with broadcaster Globo, which had long held out from licensing to the streamer in its home market even as its content appeared on Netflix elsewhere in Latin America and around the world.

Hoichoi launched in 2017 as the first venture from SVF’s new media arm and is run by co-founder Vishnu Mohta, also SVF’s executive director.

The platform hosts more than 2,000 hours of programming, among them over 100 original series, films, shorts and docuseries, and says it reaches more than 250 million Bengalis around the world.

It moved into theatrical production in 2023, setting up Hoichoi Studios as its film production arm.

item.title: How Sri Lanka pulled off the impossible
item.media:keywords: Cricket, Sri Lanka, England, Dasun Shanaka, Pavan Rathnayake
item.description: Kusal Mendis reveals the thinking behind the remarkable victory over England, including the decision to promote Dasun Shanaka
item.content:encoded:
Chasing 430 against England, Sri Lanka were already in trouble at 24-2. Their captain had been run out without facing a ball, and Harry Brook's record-breaking double-century had left them with a seemingly impossible task.

Yet inside the Sri Lankan dressing room, the belief never wavered, according to captain Kusal Mendis.

"Everyone believed we can do it," Mendis said after Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in men's one-day international history in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

The team had regularly discussed the importance of showing character and backing themselves, he said.

Sri Lanka reached 430-8 with one ball remaining to win by two wickets, comfortably surpassing their previous highest successful ODI chase of 322.

The comeback began with Avishka Fernando and Pavan Rathnayake, who put on 166 for the third wicket after the early dismissals of Kamindu Mendis and Kusal.

Fernando struck 97 off 83 balls before falling just short of a century, while Rathnayake went on to make 130 off 106 deliveries.

But a key tactical decision helped turn the chase in Sri Lanka's favour.

Mendis said he and the coach had discussed the need to approach the opening overs normally before adjusting their strategy to the enormous target. They also decided to promote Dasun Shanaka to No 5.

The move paid off spectacularly.

Shanaka hammered 97 off just 50 balls, including eight sixes, sharing a 133-run partnership with Rathnayake in only 79 deliveries.

Even after both batters fell, Sri Lanka still needed 67 from the final six overs.

Janith Liyanage took charge, racing to an unbeaten 61 off 27 balls to bring the target within reach.

Sri Lanka needed eight from the final over, but Josh Tongue dismissed Dunith Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive deliveries to threaten one last twist.

Liyanage held his nerve, striking the winning six off the penultimate ball to complete an extraordinary victory.

For Mendis, who had watched the chase unfold after his early dismissal, the result vindicated his team's approach.

"Everybody showed character and took responsibility," he said, crediting the collective effort for the successful chase.

The victory eclipsed even Brook's 202 off 116 balls, the fastest double-century in ODI history, as Sri Lanka produced a chase surpassed only by South Africa's pursuit of 435 against Australia in 2006.

item.title: Indonesia wildfires threaten world's oldest cave paintings
item.media:keywords: Indonesia, cave paintings, wildfires, Sulawesi, prehistoric art, Bank Indonesia
item.description: Even without reaching the caves, heat from nearby fires can accelerate deterioration of the paintings, while smoke deposits soot that obscures them
item.content:encoded:
The world's oldest cave paintings on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi are under threat as heat and smoke from the country's worst wildfires in more than a decade risk accelerating the deterioration of the more than 67,000-year-old works of art, researchers said.

Indonesia is battling its most intense forest and land fires since 2015 as a severe El Niño drives up temperatures and reduces rainfall, leaving its forest and peatland vulnerable to fire.

While the islands of Sumatra and Borneo are the worst affected by the disaster, fires have also spread to the island of Sulawesi, including in South Sulawesi, where limestone caves house the world's oldest prehistoric art.

In a cave in South Sulawesi's Maros-Pangkep, an artwork depicting human-like figures interacting with a pig was dated by researchers from Australia's Griffith University to be at least 51,200 years old. In a cave on Muna island, off Sulawesi, a reddish-coloured hand stencil was dated to at least 67,800 years.

Near the Maros-Pangkep cave, firefighters worked to put out fires as smoke drifted over the dramatic karst landscape that is a defining feature of the national park and UNESCO Global Geopark surrounding the cave.

Firefighter Muhammad Ikfar said fires burned near the site for more than a week earlier this month and came within 800 metres (2,625 feet) of the cave.

More than 270 hectares (667 acres) of the national park burned between Sept 30 and Oct 18, Ikfar said.

"The first and most destructive effect is the heat. Even without direct fire touching the paintings, it could ruin them because it changes the temperature around the paintings and accelerates the process of corrosion," said Griffith University archaeologist Basran Burhan.

The smoke also creates soot.

"They create soot on the paintings and cover them, so that the paintings will become blurred and difficult to identify," he said.

On Thursday and Friday, firefighters were working to put out fires in other parts of the park, firefighter Ikfar said, adding that the conditions were dry with no rain yet.

"If we don't do something about this quickly, if there aren't any tactical mitigation efforts for this incident, we will lose one of the most amazing pieces of evidence of human history in Maros-Pangkep," Burhan said. "And that is a great shame."

item.title: Four charged in Apratim murder
item.media:keywords: Cumilla, Ishayat Shahriar Apratim, Apratim murder, charges
item.description: Police say the 13-year-old was beaten to death with bamboo sticks after resisting an attempt to snatch his mobile phone
item.content:encoded:
Police have pressed formal charges against four people, including two juveniles, over the murder of 13-year-old schoolboy Ishayat Shahriar Apratim in Cumilla.

The chargesheet was submitted to the court on Tuesday, Additional Superintendent of Police Lutfar Rahman said on Thursday.

Investigators allege that Apratim was beaten to death with bamboo sticks after resisting an attempt to snatch his mobile phone.

Police accused Saiful Islam Tuhin and two juveniles of direct involvement in the killing, while Siam was allegedly involved in planning the crime. All four have been arrested.

Tuhin, 19, and Siam, 19, are being held at Cumilla Central Jail, while the two minors have been sent to the Gazipur Child Development Centre.

Apratim was the only child of Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, and KM Firoz Shahriar, who is involved in the mobile phone business. He was a seventh-grade student at Border Guard Public School in Kotbari.

The schoolboy went missing after leaving home on the afternoon of Sept 18. Police recovered his body the following day from a wooded area in Sananda near the Lalmai hills.

According to investigators, Tuhin took Apratim to the secluded area and tried to snatch his iPhone.

When Apratim resisted, a scuffle broke out. Tuhin allegedly struck him on the head with a bamboo stick, followed by the two juveniles. The schoolboy died from his injuries.

Police said the three fled with Apratim's phone after making sure he was dead.

Investigators reviewed CCTV footage from surrounding areas and identified Tuhin, who had been seen with Apratim.

Police subsequently took Tuhin into custody for questioning and recovered Apratim's phone from his home. Information provided by Tuhin led investigators to the other suspects.

"My dreams of living revolved around my son. The killers have taken those dreams away," said Apratim's father, KM Firoz Shahriar, who filed the case.

"I want a speedy trial of the killers. I hope the court will hand them the maximum punishment as quickly as possible. Their age should not become a loophole allowing them to escape justice."

item.title: Heineken fears weight-loss drugs could dent beer sales
item.media:keywords: Heineken, GLP-1, weight-loss drugs, beer sales, alcohol industry
item.description: The brewer urges British pubs to promote half-pints and low-alcohol options amid signs that people taking GLP-1 drugs are drinking less
item.content:encoded:
Heineken has urged British pubs and bars to adapt to the booming use of weight-loss drugs or risk losing customers and revenue, according to a company presentation seen by Reuters, in a rare acknowledgement from a major alcohol maker that the medicines pose a threat to beer sales.

The warning comes as GLP-1 use has surged, with some 10 million people taking medications like Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy in the US last year, according to JPMorgan research.

Their growth is having ramifications across the consumer goods industry, hitting cravings for sweets and snacks, driving up demand for clothing alterations and prompting a scramble to sell products that counter side-effects.

Heineken, the world's second-largest brewer after AB InBev told hospitality customers that GLP-1 drugs can reduce the desire to drink and put pressure on beer and cider sales from "fullness and fewer serves", while warning that traditional multi-pint drinking occasions could become harder to sustain.

The previously unreported presentation, sent to hospitality customers this month, advised venues to promote half-pints, low- and no-alcohol drinks and pair drinks with small plates, or risk declines in customer visits and spending as use of the medicines becomes increasingly mainstream in Britain.

The alcohol industry is already grappling with years of falling sales in some major markets as consumers cut back on drinking for health and economic reasons.

Heineken told Reuters the presentation was shared as part of its regular engagement with UK hospitality businesses to help them understand how the market is evolving.

"We see some changes in consumption behaviour among (GLP-1) users and will continue to monitor how these behaviours evolve in 2027," Heineken said.

GLP-1 users were not abandoning alcohol altogether but were increasingly opting for smaller serves, lower-alcohol drinks and more premium products, aligning with broader ongoing trends, it continued, adding its portfolio is well positioned to meet these demands.

EVIDENCE OF REDUCED CONSUMPTION GROWS

Europe is the Dutch brewer's largest market by revenue, but growth has been sluggish. Heineken has singled out Britain, where it owns more than 2,000 pubs, as a relative bright spot.

Beer generated nearly £14 billion of sales in British pubs, bars and restaurants in the year to February 2026, with less than £300 million of that from no- and low-alcohol beers, according to a Heineken UK report.

Although drinks companies have largely played down the threat from GLP-1 medicines, emerging spending data points to an impact on purchases.

A group of US households with a GLP-1 user tracked by market research firm Circana between 2024 and 2026 reduced spending on alcohol for both at-home and out-of-home consumption compared with households without a user.

After two years on the drugs, they spent about 7 percent less per month on alcohol versus non-using households, including around 13.5 percent less on beer.

Top spirits maker Diageo has told investors any impact from GLP-1 drugs should be manageable even if use becomes more widespread.

Carlsberg told Reuters existing data did not yet support the view that the drugs were a clear driver of beer consumption trends. Anheuser-Busch InBev declined to comment.

Surveys in Europe and the UK by Circana, market researcher NIQ and specialist UK-based hospitality researcher KAM have also pointed to reduced drinking by GLP-1 users.

Ten of 11 GLP-1 users Reuters interviewed said they had reduced their drinking, sometimes significantly, saying it left them feeling uncomfortable or unwell, or they simply no longer had any desire to drink.

UK-based Daniel Cornell, founder of hospitality executive recruitment business SPE Resourcing, said he used to drink regularly at work events and on weekends but now finds alcohol causes him discomfort and results in a multi-day hangover.

GLP-1's effects on the brain may also affect users' motivation to drink, said Joseph Schacht, a professor at the University of Colorado Anschutz, who led a randomised controlled trial on the impact of GLP-1s on people with alcohol use disorder. He said trials have consistently shown a reduction in cravings and consumption for people with AUD.

Schacht said the medicines could create a potential "Prozac moment" for AUD treatment, while also posing a challenge for alcohol producers if broader groups of drinkers cut back too.

item.title: Aliss reported for suspect bowling action
item.media:keywords: Aliss Al Islam, suspect bowling action, Afghanistan vs Bangladesh
item.description: The Bangladesh off-spinner must undergo an independent assessment after match officials raise concerns during the Afghanistan clash
item.content:encoded:
Bangladesh off-spinner Aliss Al Islam has been reported for a suspect bowling action following his ODI debut against Afghanistan in the tri-nation series in Sharjah.

The International Cricket Council (ICC) confirmed the development on Thursday, saying match officials had raised concerns over the legality of his action during Wednesday's match.

Aliss must now undergo an independent assessment at an ICC-accredited testing centre to determine whether his bowling action complies with international regulations.

The referral does not amount to a suspension, and he can continue bowling pending the assessment.

The 29-year-old endured a difficult ODI debut, conceding 47 runs in 8.3 overs without taking a wicket as Bangladesh suffered a seven-wicket defeat and crashed out of the tri-series.

It is not the first time Aliss has faced scrutiny over his bowling action.

He was reported during the 2019 Bangladesh Premier League (BPL), shortly after taking a hat-trick on his debut for Dhaka Dynamites.

He subsequently underwent remedial work and passed an assessment, receiving clearance to bowl in domestic cricket.

Aliss was reported again during the 2025 BPL but cleared another assessment conducted by the Bangladesh Cricket Board.

item.title: Experimental cancer vaccine shows promise in trial
item.description: The experimental treatment is tailored to each patient's tumour and given alongside an existing immunotherapy drug
item.content:encoded:
A personalised mRNA cancer vaccine, used alongside an existing immunotherapy drug, has been linked to a 42 percent reduction in the risk of melanoma returning or patients dying after surgery, according to clinical trial results.

Patients who received the experimental vaccine, called intismeran autogene, together with the approved immunotherapy drug Keytruda, had a 42 percent lower risk of cancer recurrence or death compared with those who received Keytruda alone, CNN reports.

The vaccine uses the same mRNA technology that underpins Moderna's COVID-19 shot, but instead of targeting a virus, it is designed to help the immune system recognise and attack cancer cells.

It is custom-built for each patient: after surgery removes the tumour, a sample is sequenced and the vaccine is tailored to genetic markers most likely to trigger an immune response.

"This personalised cancer vaccine boosts the body's immune response only against the cancer cells that are there," Dr Michael Postow, chief of the melanoma service at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, told CNN. "It is a much more targeted immune boost directly against that patient's individual tumour."

Developers Merck and Moderna said they are engaging with regulatory authorities following the results. Analysts at RBC Capital Markets expect the US Food and Drug Administration to approve the therapy next year, although no approval has yet been granted.

The companies are also testing the technology against lung and pancreatic cancers.

The results were presented at a meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology in Madrid and are based on a median follow-up of around two years.

The trial is continuing to assess overall survival, with the companies noting a "favourable trend" but saying it is too early to draw conclusions, CNN reported.

Despite the findings, Moderna's shares fell 18 percent on Thursday, with analysts pointing out that the results were slightly less striking than those of an earlier, smaller trial. Even so, the stock remains up more than 500 percent year-to-date.

item.title: Grief as Houthi attack victim's body returns home
item.media:keywords: Bangladesh, Saudi Arabia, Riyadh airport, Md Shahed Ahmed, Houthi attack
item.description: Shahed's family receives immediate financial assistance, with further payments and benefits under consideration
item.content:encoded:
The body of Md Shahed Ahmed, who was killed in a missile attack in Saudi Arabia, has arrived in Bangladesh.

A US-Bangla Airlines flight carrying his body from Jeddah landed at Dhaka's Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 8:22am on Friday.

Shahed's loved ones received his body at the airport in the presence of State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam.

His family received Tk 85,000 in immediate financial assistance through the Wage Earners' Welfare Board, including Tk 35,000 for burial and transportation expenses and a special grant of Tk 50,000, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment said on Friday.

His employer, Saad Al-Essa Contracting Company, has also deposited 27,395 Saudi riyals, equivalent to around Tk 900,000, in outstanding wages, allowances and service benefits into the Bangladesh Embassy's account in Riyadh.

The money will be handed over to the family through the Wage Earners' Welfare Board, the ministry said.

The family may receive another Tk 300,000, subject to verification of Shahed's BMET card or other valid identification documents. They may also qualify for an additional Tk 1 million in insurance benefits.

Yemen's Houthi group attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh around 3:15pm on Oct 10.

The attack reportedly killed 13 people of different nationalities and injured 308 others. Two Bangladeshis were among the dead, while 27 were injured.

Shahed was from Madla village in Bogura's Shajahanpur.

The other Bangladeshi killed was Md Nasrullah Badarpuri, an Umrah visa holder from Badarpur village in Cumilla's Nangalkot. He had been waiting in Riyadh for a connecting flight to Jeddah.

item.title: Japan to simulate cyberattacks amid PHP flaw fallout
item.media:keywords: Japan, cybersecurity, PHP vulnerability, SoftBank, AI
item.description: Attackers are likely targeting Japanese businesses for their detailed records, which are “no longer protected by a language barrier” because of AI
item.content:encoded:
Japan said on Friday it will set up a team to simulate cyberattacks using AI to identify weaknesses in technology systems as organisations scramble to curtail risks from flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet.

Government and company websites across the world went offline this week after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used programming language prompted millions of hacking attempts, forcing website operators to rush to protect or temporarily shut down their systems.

Highlighting the extent of the disruption, Japanese mobile carrier SoftBank said on Friday it was suspending its emergency alert system for mobile users.

That means customers will not receive early warnings for earthquakes, tsunami alerts or disaster and evacuation information as the system undergoes maintenance to address a PHP vulnerability, SoftBank said.

"An attack can succeed by getting through just one hole ... for that reason it's important we shift our mindset and think from the perspective of the attacker," Japanese industry minister Ryosei Akazawa said on Friday.

"Defenders also need to make use of AI and respond proactively, staying one step ahead."

Emergency shutdowns this week from Tokyo to Helsinki of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services marked one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running.

Companies including brokerage Nomura, lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, airline ANA and East Japan Railway (JR East) temporarily suspended some internet services as part of emergency measures.

Japan's Ministry of Finance, National Tax Agency and Meteorological Agency also suspended some online services.

On Friday, JR East said some group services had resumed while others would be restored once confirmed safe. Nippon Paint said it had applied a security patch as a precaution and its website is back online.

Attackers are likely targeting Japanese businesses for their thorough records, which are no longer protected by a language barrier because of AI, said Eva Chen, CEO of Trend Micro.

Japan has been too comfortable with its existing infrastructure, which it felt was safe enough, she said.

Cybersecurity experts have said AI is helping attackers automate tasks from scanning for software vulnerabilities to crafting phishing campaigns, making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect.

The developers of PHP - a computing language like HTML and Python - released fixes on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI. They urged users to "update immediately."

item.title: Final homecoming for Bangladeshi killed in Houthi attack
item.media:keywords: Saudia Arabia, Houthi attack, migrant worker
item.description: The body of Bangladeshi worker Shahed Ahmed, killed in a Houthi attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, arrived in Dhaka on Friday. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam handed over his remains to the family at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, where scenes of grief unfolded as his wife and children received his coffin.

item.title: Asian shares wobble as tech rout boosts bonds
item.description: Nasdaq slumps over 2 percent overnight as AI bubble fears grow
item.content:encoded:
Asian shares fell on Friday as concerns over the enormous funding needs of AI hammered tech and led to the biggest daily rally in Treasuries in more than three years, with investors fleeing to sovereign bonds and safe-haven currencies.

Markets also sharply pared back expectations of further policy tightening from the Federal Reserve, stripping out almost a full quarter-point rate hike for next year amid concerns a bursting AI bubble could derail the data-centre investment boom and hobble the US economy. A December rate rise is no longer fully priced, with the implied probability falling to 85 percent .

That was despite elevated oil prices, with Brent hitting a five-month peak at $114 a barrel on Friday. Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns of further disruption to energy supplies as fears grow that the conflict in West Asia could escalate sharply.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan fell 0.3 percent on Friday, bringing its weekly loss to 2.7 percent and marking a fourth straight week in the red. Japan's Nikkei dropped 1.3 percent and was down a whopping 5 percent for the week.

South Korea's KOSPI skidded 1.7 percent, on course for a 4.3 percent weekly decline, with memory chipmaker SK Hynix down 2.5 percent on the day. Taiwan's stock market was closed due to a typhoon.

An index of mainland Chinese blue chips lost 1.1percent on Friday to hit the lowest level since July 2025. The index was down about 20 percent from its peak in late June. Hong Kong's Hang Seng edged up 0.1 percent after dropping 3 percent on Thursday.

"AI is under the cosh," said Charlie McElligott, managing director for cross-asset strategy at Nomura Securities International in New York, in a note.

"US Treasury bonds are — gasp — working as your hedge again, as the market seems to be real-time repricing the probabilities of a US growth scare off the back of the AI reset."

On Wall Street, the Nasdaq slumped more than 2percent as Meta shares lost nearly 8percent after the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to its AI-related expenditures, and announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on the technology.

Tesla shares fell 3.1percent as the electric car maker cut its 2026 capital spending plans.

"The question is whether selling accelerates or markets stage another familiar reversal," said Chris Weston, head of Research at Pepperstone.

"There's nothing more emotive than a falling market where buyers refuse to engage. Sellers don't need a fresh catalyst when deteriorating price action itself encourages more selling."

Treasuries Shine

As equities tumbled, money flowed into safe-haven US Treasuries, sending yields plunging across the curve overnight. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield slid more than 19 basis points, the biggest drop since March 2023, before steadying at 4.9591percent on Friday, back below the closely watched 5percent level.

That was also due in part to the ongoing sell-off in French bonds, whose benchmark yield climbed 6 basis points overnight to 5.0601percent , the highest level since 2002.

"The US 10yr yield gapped back below 5percent with some conviction. We're not convinced it keeps on going," said Padhraic Garvey, ING's regional head of research for the Americas.

"We're minded to expect it to snap back above (5percent ), as we still have inflation/fiscal deficit/AI boom underpinnings to navigate. And we have the US midterm elections approaching as an excuse for trouble. But it will need some degree of calm in the risk space first."

The 2-year Treasury yield slumped nearly 19 bps overnight and were last flat at 4.6566 percent .

Government bonds in Asia also rallied. The yield on 10-year Japanese government bonds fell 9 basis points to 2.790 percent, while Australia's 10-year yield dropped 10 bps to 5.164 percent .

In currency markets, safe havens such as the yen and Swiss franc gained. The dollar fell 0.2 percent to 156.44 yen on Friday, after slumping 0.9 percent overnight.

The dollar also slipped 0.1 percent to 0.8196 Swiss francs, the lowest in a month, after an overnight fall of 0.5 percent .

Gold failed to catch any safe-haven demand though, and was flat at $4,021.99 an ounce on Friday after a nearly 3 percent drop overnight.
